newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends firmer in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends firmer in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen interest rate futures settled slightly firmer on Friday after activity slowed in the afternoon ahead of a three-day weekend.
The December firmed in early trade on continued short-covering from dealers given the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) very accommodative credit stance for a second day.
But its rise was capped at 99.04 on a large-lot selling after Japan's March unemployment rate showed an improvement.
Japan's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate fell to 3.2 percent in March, down from 3.3 percent in February and its lowest level in 12 months, the government said on Friday.

"Large-lot selling probably from Japanese banks hit the contract when the jobs data was released," said a city bank dealer. "But follow-through selling did not appear amid a lack of fresh factors suggesting higher interest rates," he said.

The December later dipped to 98.99 on light selling after falls in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures. But a majority were sidelined as their positions had been squared ahead of the key U.S. payroll data later on Friday and a long weekend.
The Tokyo market is closed for a holiday on Monday.
The December settled up 0.01 at 99.01 after opening at 99.02. Turnover was 67,400 contracts.
The price at 99.00 shows the market has factored in a 0.5 point rise in the BOJ's discount rate, now at a record low 0.5 percent, by the October-December period, traders said.

But a trust bank dealer said the market is expected to be vulnerable to falls for the time being. "If concerns over higher U.S. interest rates do not hurt Wall Street and/or inflation fears spread in Japan from weaker yen, the December contract may fall to 98.95 next week," he said.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate fell to 0.47 percent from Thursday's 0.50 percent.
The BOJ left the market in surplus of some 300 billion yen after its morning operation for a second day on Friday. This compared with a 200 billion yen surplus in the previous days.
"The operations today and yesterday showed the BOJ wanted to keep the key overnight rate below the discount rate on average in this bank reserve period," said another bank dealer.
Long-end benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.57 and 0.56 percent, against Thursday's 0.56 percent. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
